tasks.short: Check diet changes with the ward, check trays against diets, deliver them, confirm the patient at the bedside and note refused meals.

steps.what: Food server phones the ward to check diet changes since the morning list
Food server checks each tray against the diet list before leaving the kitchen
Food server delivers trays to patients' rooms
Food server checks name and wristband so meals reach the correct recipients
Food server notes refused or missed meals on paper

tasks.design: Diet orders entered by ward nurses in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) flow to the meal system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) as they change, so the diet list is current and fewer calls to the ward are needed. Each tray carries a printed label; scanning it at the kitchen exit checks it against the patient's current diet and allergies, and the server looks at mismatches only. Refused meals are noted with a pick list on a tablet. Delivering and checking the patient at the bedside stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diet lists were printed in the morning and trays checked by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Meal systems take diet orders from the record and check scanned tray labels against them.
tasks.still_hard: Late diet changes and patients who moved rooms still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a patient on a liquid diet has a sandwich on the bedside table.

reach.learn: Whether diet orders reach the kitchen in time.

evidence.claim: Hospital meal systems take diet orders from the record and check scanned tray labels against them.
Food businesses must inform people about 14 allergens in unpacked food.
Diet orders are health data; access must be limited to care and kitchen staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diet list to noted refusals; meal production is outside.
Input contract: diet orders entered by ward nurses in the record; prepared trays from the kitchen; fallback is the printed list.
Delivery and bedside checks do not change.
Nurse time is outside the server's savings.
unknowns: Diet changes per day after the morning list.

incremental.description: Food server learns the scanner and tablet.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is delivering trays in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take meal orders at the bedside, check them against diets, pass them to the kitchen, answer questions about dishes and phone late changes.

steps.what: Food server visits patients to take food orders from the menu card
Food server checks orders against each patient's diet and allergies
Food server resolves orders the diet check flags with the patient
Food server relays orders to the kitchen by typing them in or phoning
Food server answers patients' questions about dishes and ingredients
Food server phones the kitchen about late changes

tasks.design: Patients who can order themselves use the bedside screen, which shows only dishes that fit their diet order and lists allergens per dish from the recipe records in the meal system ({OPS_SYSTEM}); the server takes orders in person only from patients who need help, on a tablet with the same filter. Orders go straight to the kitchen screen. Answering questions and late changes stay with the server.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were taken on paper cards, checked against diet lists by eye and typed in or phoned.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital menus filter by diet, show allergens and send orders to the kitchen.
tasks.still_hard: Many patients are too ill or confused to order on a screen.
tasks.human_edge: Finding something a patient with no appetite will still eat.

reach.learn: Whether residents use a filtered menu.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere lets guests read item descriptions and allergen information and order; orders go to the kitchen through the POS.
Allergen information may be given in speech if a notice says guests can ask.

assumptions: Boundary: from the menu to orders in the kitchen; cooking is outside.
Input contract: diet orders entered by ward nurses; recipes and allergens kept by the kitchen in the meal system; fallback is paper cards.
Questions and late changes do not change.
Patients' time is outside the server's savings.
Input contract for s2: diet orders entered by ward nurses in the meal system as part of admission today; the diet filter needs no new entry.
unknowns: Share of patients able to order on the bedside screen.
research_questions: Do order errors fall with the diet filter?

incremental.description: Food server helps patients with the bedside screen.
Patients who can order themselves pick meals on the bedside screen.

approvals.approved_version: Orders as confirmed by the food server after the diet check; a later change goes by phone in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards where most patients need help save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch serving and portioning, probe food temperatures, log them, correct colleagues and report repeated problems.

steps.what: Food server watches serving techniques and portioning on the line
Food server checks food temperatures with a probe
Food server writes temperatures on the paper food safety sheet
Food server corrects colleagues on the spot so proper procedures are followed
Food server reports repeated problems to the supervisor

tasks.design: A wireless probe logs each reading with time and product to the food safety app on a tablet ({OTHER}), replacing the paper sheet. Watching serving, probing food, correcting colleagues and reporting stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Temperatures were written by hand on paper sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Wireless probes log readings to food safety apps.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting poor technique is judgement; no sensor sees it.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a colleague use the same tongs for two diets.

reach.learn: Whether logged probes fill gaps in records.

evidence.claim: Wireless probes log temperature readings to food safety apps.
Food businesses must keep records of their critical food safety checks.

assumptions: Boundary: from watching the line to reporting; supervisor follow-up is outside.
Input contract: products and limits set by the kitchen manager in the app; fallback is the paper sheet.
Watching, probing and correcting do not change.
Readings are about food, not used to rate staff.
research_questions: Are temperature records complete more often?

incremental.description: Food server charges and pairs the probe.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is watching in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record special items served, total them per shift, enter totals for ordering and billing, list items not served and tell the dietitian about refusals.

steps.what: Food server records amounts and types of special food items served on the paper ward list
Food server tallies the list per item at the end of the shift
Food server enters the totals in the kitchen spreadsheet for ordering and billing
Food server compares the list with the orders to find items not served
Food server tells the dietitian about patients who refuse supplements

tasks.design: The server taps each special item served (supplement drinks, tube feeds, diet products) on a tablet per patient in the meal system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), where the dietitian's orders already sit. The system totals the shift, passes totals to kitchen ordering and billing, and lists ordered items not served. Telling the dietitian about refusals stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Items were written on paper ward lists, tallied by hand and typed into a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Meal systems hold special item orders per patient and record what was served on a tablet.
tasks.still_hard: Taps must be made at the bedside, not from memory at the end of the round.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing why a patient left the supplement and telling the dietitian.

reach.learn: Whether served-item records change diet plans sooner.

evidence.claim: Meal systems record items served per patient on a tablet and total them.
Per-server logs can count as a facility to monitor performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from special item orders to totals and the dietitian informed; diet plans are outside.
Input contract: special item orders entered by the dietitian in the meal system; fallback is the paper ward list.
Telling the dietitian does not change.
Records are about patients' intake, not used to rate servers.
research_questions: Do billing differences for special items fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards without tablets on the trolley keep paper lists.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The food server keeps delivery, bedside checks and conversations; lists, tallies and phone checks shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the tray scanner and tablet
role.ambitious_version: A server who spends more time with patients who eat poorly.
